mutation_battery.note: Fourteen mutations, every one fires on the condition it names. Four are worth naming because they are the ones a reader would otherwise have to take on trust. `grading-4` replaces provider-keyed ingestion provenance with the cheaper flat two-value allow-list and test 76 fails -- which is what makes admitting `operator` to the trusted set a widening rather than a loosening, since under a flat list an `operator` event could claim `ingestor.cycle`. `couple-2` catches that same loosening from the opposite side, by pointing the READER's required source for `operator` at `ingestor.cycle` and failing the writer/reader coupling assertion. `grading-2` disables the result-market-key guard and tests 72 and 73 fail, proving the 280 production `points-all-game-ml` score rows are refused rather than merely unlikely to be selected. `stats-1` folds an unrecognised settlement result into `pending`, and test 19 fails -- the silent-forever failure mode. An earlier, weaker form of the help-drift mutation did NOT fire, and that is recorded rather than smoothed over: replacing `--evidence` in only the flag list left it present in the worked example lower in USAGE, so the mutation was ineffective rather than the test blind; `help-1` is the corrected form, which replaces every occurrence and fires.

production_measurement.target: production zfzdnfwdarxucxtaojxm, read-only, governed -- one SELECT, no write, no containment setting touched
production_measurement.note: The cohort predicate is `metadata ? 'distributionMode'` and it returns exactly one row: Griff's Milestone 1 pick dfcd9486-cba2-4bb5-b684-beec36e52c0b. Two of these numbers decide a design choice rather than describe the world. 280 rows under `points-all-game-ml` carry a raw score and ZERO of them carry a participant_id, so no side is attached and the number's meaning is ambiguous -- which is why the attested win flag gets the dedicated key `game_moneyline_win` instead. And there are ZERO rows under that dedicated key today, so this change makes no pre-existing row newly interpretable: it can only read a result an operator writes after it lands. The 0 outbox rows are the containment observation, and this lane adds no path to a non-zero value.

journey_output.what: What the new aggregate prints for the real cohort, today and after the pick is attested as a win.
journey_output.note: 3 units at -110 risks 3 to win 3 * (100/110) = 2.7273. `roi: null` rather than 0 in the pending case is the load-bearing half: 0% is indistinguishable from a genuine break-even, and reporting it would be wrong in the reassuring direction.

coverage_gap.statement: The staging job is green and exercises none of this lane's changed paths. The 19 live suites wired at this head were written for other lanes, and this lane deliberately wires no twentieth. The reason is that a live suite here would have to seed its own events, event_participants and game_results rows under market_key game_moneyline_win -- and production holds zero such rows and 280 points-all-game-ml rows with no participant_id, so the suite would be proving that the seed it just wrote can be read back, not that the journey works. Asserting the seed would read as coverage and would be worth nothing.
coverage_gap.why_that_is_the_honest_position_and_not_: The live suites exist to prove that a real driver behaves as the in-memory one is assumed to. The three code paths here make no new database call and no new query shape: grading reads `game_results` through the same repository method it already used, and the stats aggregate is a pure function over rows the report already fetched with `select: '*'`. What WOULD need live proof is a result actually written under `game_moneyline_win` -- and there are zero such rows in production or staging, because writing one is an operator action under DB_ENVIRONMENT_OPERATOR_POLICY.md that this lane deliberately does not perform. Claiming live coverage by seeding a row would prove the seed, not the journey.

what_is_unproven: that a real operator attestation written by scripts/ops/track-only/operator-attest-result.ts --apply lands rows PostgREST will return in the shape validateEventProvenanceForGrading expects
that the grading pass, running against real Postgres, settles a Track Only moneyline end to end from those rows

coverage_gap.why_it_matters: These are the three joins between halves that were built separately. The static proof covers each half and the cross-file assertion added at 2b0a01e02 covers the one contract they share (the market key and the operator provenance pair), which is the join that could drift silently. What remains unproven is the database round trip, and the honest way to close it is a real operator attestation against a real event -- an operator action under DB_ENVIRONMENT_OPERATOR_POLICY.md, not an agent one.

binding.binding_rule: lane_source_tree_run: a pull_request-triggered run at head 139187832. That head is not necessarily the current PR head -- writing a receipt into a proof bundle moves the head, so no bundle can ever cite a run at its own head. The claim made instead is one that does not go stale: every commit on this lane after 2b0a01e02 (= sha_binding.verified_source_sha) touches only docs/06_status/proof/UTV2-1889/, so every such head compiles a source tree byte-identical to the bound head's. Checkable with `git diff --name-only 2b0a01e02 <any later head on this lane>`, which returns proof-directory files and nothing else. `verify` and `Writable DB proof (staging only)` are asserted green on the MERGE SHA by closeout check G6, which is where the route B deferral is actually enforced.
